{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.4 (TrueLink Hosting, Support and Interface Agreement)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Client-side) 
**Re:** Playbook review — verified findings only

## Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against the playbook. The commercial architecture on term, termination, exclusivity and audit is genuinely favourable to us — we have an unconditional convenience-termination right on roughly 30–60 days' notice, a one-year auto-renewing term with a mutual 30-day non-renewal notice, an expressly non-exclusive licence with confirmation that we are "not obligated to utilize the License," no non-compete, no non-solicit, no minimum-purchase penalty mechanics, no audit rights running against us, and a Vendor-side most-favoured-rate commitment plus a first-year price freeze. Governing law and venue (California; San Luis Obispo County) sit at our fallback and we do not propose changing them.

The risk is concentrated in the protection package we would normally expect from a hosting vendor that holds our Web Site, Client Content and borrower Credit Data. Three critical deviations drive our position: there is **no Vendor IP infringement indemnity** (Section 12(b) is a breach-of-contract indemnity only, against a broad Client-side indemnity in 12(a)); the **only liability limitation is one-sided**, capping TrueLink at 12 months' compensation while leaving our very broad indemnity entirely uncapped and with no exclusion of indirect damages; and **ownership is one-way**, with §2(d) reserving TrueLink's rights in the Interface and nothing affirming our rights in Client Content, our IP, our borrower/loan data, or the Support Services results we pay for. Alongside these, the licence grant does not reach our affiliates or contractors and cannot follow us through an M&A transaction, there is **no TrueLink performance warranty** (only a Y2K warranty) against an implied-warranty disclaimer, **no exit/transition or data-return-and-deletion obligation**, and **no insurance covenant of any kind**.

We have redlined the four critical/high deviations, the warranty and transition gaps, and inserted an insurance section. We have not touched the clauses that benefit us.

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 2 LICENSE. |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 2 LICENSE. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Compliant | § 2 LICENSE. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § 2 LICENSE. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 12 INDEMNITY. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | Compliant | § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § 12 INDEMNITY. |

### Redlines proposed

- **INDEMN (§12):** Add a TrueLink indemnity for third-party IP infringement, breach of law, data/security incidents and gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with the standard notice/control/cooperation procedure. We have not narrowed Client's §12(a) indemnity in this pass.
- **IP (§2):** Insert a new §2(e) reserving Client Content, Client IP and our data, assigning Support Services work product to us, and licensing back any embedded TrueLink IP. Note that §10 makes Client IP and "all results of the Hosting and Support Services" confidential, which is secrecy only and not ownership.
- **LOL-CAP (§12):** Make the cap mutual and Agreement-wide at the greater of 12 months' compensation and USD 1,000,000, exclude indirect and consequential damages, and place indemnification, confidentiality/data security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement outside the cap; Client payment obligations preserved. Fallback: a straight mutual 12-months'-fees cap with indemnity/confidentiality/gross negligence carve-outs. We also flag that the existing cap is limited to "Sections 3, 4, 7 and 11," none of which appear as headings, so even the Vendor-side cap is of uncertain scope.
- **ASSIGN (§15):** Add an affiliate/successor carve-out for Client, a "not unreasonably withheld" standard on consent, and a bar on TrueLink transferring to a Client competitor, preserving the existing mutual structure.
- **LICENSE (§2(a), §15):** Extend the grant to Client's affiliates and contractors and permit transfer to a successor in an M&A transaction. Fallback on scope: affiliates covered on written notice.
- **WARRANTY (§9):** Add an express TrueLink performance and conformance warranty (professional and workmanlike services; Interface conforms to documentation) with a repair/replace/refund remedy, at 12 months for software. Fallback: 90 days software / 30 days services.
- **TRANSITION (§14):** Insert up to six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, return of Client Content and Credit Data in a commonly used machine-readable format within 30 days, then deletion with written certification. Survival is carried by §24 (Sections 1 and 5–30 survive). Fallback: 90 days' assistance plus export within 30 days.
- **INSURANCE (new §31):** CGL USD 1M per occurrence / USD 2M aggregate, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request. Fallback: E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M.

## Walk-away items

1. **One-sided liability cap (LOL-CAP, §12).** Our liability — including the broad §12(a) indemnity covering any breach, any Client Content claim and product/service injury claims — is entirely uncapped while TrueLink's is capped at 12 months' compensation. This is squarely within the rule's walk-away territory ("Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped") and is compounded by the absence of any indirect/consequential damages exclusion. Mutuality is not tradeable.
2. **No Vendor insurance at all (INSURANCE).** TrueLink hosts the Web Site, receives and uploads Client Content and transmits and archives borrower/loan-applicant Credit Data from TransUnion, Equifax and Experian. A vendor processing personal financial data with no insurance is walk-away territory under the rule, and the gap is unfunded: the §12(b) indemnity has no coverage behind it and TrueLink's exposure is capped.

**Approaching walk-away (must move, not yet a walk):**

- **Warranty (§9/§12).** With only a Y2K warranty on the TrueLink side and an implied-warranty disclaimer carved back only "except as expressly set forth in this Agreement," the practical result approaches an "AS IS" position.
- **Assignment (§15).** An unqualified consent standard with no successor/M&A carve-out approaches the walk-away position of a prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out.
- **Vendor IP indemnity (§12).** The complete absence of an IP infringement indemnity fails even the fallback and, given the Interface is TrueLink's, is not something we can absorb.

## Next steps

1. Send the redline with the four critical/high deviations (INDEMN, IP, LOL-CAP, ASSIGN/LICENSE) presented as a package and identified as our conditions to signature; hold mutuality of the liability cap and the IP indemnity firm.
2. Table the warranty, transition/data-return and insurance inserts together as the "hosting vendor standard" package, with the stated fallbacks available (90/30-day warranty; 90 days' transition; E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M).
3. **Complete the blanks before signature:** the minimum monthly fee in §5(a) ("not less than $____ per month") and the Support Services minimum period in §4 ("not less than ____ months"). The §4 blank matters because §14's "Subject to Section 4" carve-out could otherwise be argued to qualify our convenience right as to Support Services; confirm the minimums align with the one-month termination runway.
4. **Fix the cross-references:** §13's reference to "Section 12" for termination (termination is §14; §12 is indemnity); §6's reference to "the minimum monthly fees listed in Section 4" (they are in §5(a)); and the §12 cap's reference to "Sections 3, 4, 7 and 11," which do not correspond to headings in the document.
5. **Diligence the separate Non-Competition Agreement** referenced at the Credit Data licence (§8(d)). In this document it operates as a limitation on TrueLink's licensed use of Credit Data, which is acceptable, but it is a separate instrument we have not reviewed and we should confirm it contains no reciprocal restraint on Client.
6. Low-priority ask, to be raised with the fee schedule rather than under the renewal rule: a CPI-or-3% cap on renewal uplift. §6 freezes Hosting Services costs for the first year and gives us a most-favoured-rate commitment, but leaves renewal uplift uncapped.
7. Do not volunteer a mutual non-solicit or any exclusivity/sourcing commitment; the current silence favours us. If TrueLink raises a non-solicit, hold it to the fallback (services personnel only, 12 months from end of involvement, general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs, no no-hire)."}
